Proposition
[Pullback metric] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0411 1. appG:G.3\group Metric spaces For a map $f:X\to (Y,d_Y)$, the pullback $f^*d_Y(x,x')=d_Y(f(x),f(x'))$ is a pseudo-metric on $X$; it is a metric when $f$ is injective.
Proof

\sketch Nonnegativity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality are inherited from $d_Y$. If $f$ is injective, $f(x)=f(x')$ implies $x=x'$, so the separation axiom also holds.

□
